headline: Lowell alcohol rules for bars and restaurants approved, including new permit for 18-to-20-year-old events.
summary: Restaurants must serve suitable food at all hours of alcohol service, and can be asked to prove food sales are at least 35% of annual revenue, down from 40% in the first draft. General on-premises licensees need a special one-day permit to admit anyone under 21. License change applications are due January 29th, 2027, at 12:00 noon. Complaints against Lowell Pawn, Sokha Pawn Brokers, and Club Passe-Temps were referred to police.
decisions: Approved four one-day licenses for wines and malt beverages at Hive Public Market, 101 Paige Street.
Approved two one-day licenses for Lowell Community Charter Public School events at 250 Jackson Street.
Approved special event permit for 18- to 20-year-olds at Tuscabar Performance Center, 72 Middlesex Street, on November 18th, 2026.
Approved common victualler license for Corner Crust & Crumb, Inc., at 165 Chelmsford Street.
Approved Class 2 dealer license for Angels Auto Care at 45 Meadowcroft Street, Unit 1.
Approved Section 1 on regulations for bars and restaurants, four in favor, none opposed.
Approved the special 18 to 20 event permit procedures in Section 2.
Approved Section 3 on manager and promoter responsibilities, four in favor, none opposed.
Approved January 29th, 2027, at 12:00 noon as the deadline to submit license change applications.
Continued the public hearing on the Showcase Cinema Lowell license transfer to the November 19th, 2026, meeting.
Referred complaint about Lowell Pawn at 755 Lakeview Avenue to the Lowell Police Department for investigation.
Referred complaint about Sokha Pawn Brokers at 28 Branch Street to the police department.
Referred complaint about Club Passe-Temps of Lowell at 369-371 Moody Street to the Lowell Police Department.
discussion: Restaurant food rules: The Law Department said restaurants must serve suitable food at all hours of alcohol service. After feedback, the food-sales cutoff for restaurants was changed from 40% to 35% of annual revenue.
Under-21 event permit: Members asked whether the 18 to 20 permit should have an hour limit. The Law Department said the draft has none, and the commission could add one later by amendment.

License change deadline: Changes must also go through the ABCC, which may take 4 months after the application date. Members set January 29th, 2027, at 12:00 noon as the deadline for license change applications.
Menu change rule: Members asked what counts as a substantial menu change. The Law Department said the rule targets a licensee that stops serving food, not minor menu tweaks.

Complaint review: Three complaints were referred to police. The Law Department's preliminary review found some fall outside the commission's jurisdiction, and a report is expected at the next meeting.
